items.title: Microsoft stock just cleared a big hurdle but still trails the S&P 500
items.summary: The bulls are back in control of Microsoft stock.

items.title: Palantir and These Software Stocks Slide in Seesaw With Chip Giants
items.summary: Palantir slid 1.3% and Microsoft dipped 0.7% in the premarket.  Salesforce ServiceNow  and  Workday  were among the other software stocks trading in the red.  The moves came as shares of chip and optical networking companies rallied, following a strong batch of earnings reports that signaled to the market that demand for AI remains robust.

items.title: Nvidia Stock Rises as CEO Eases AI Debt Fears
items.summary: Nvidia  stock was rising in premarket trading Wednesday as fears over the company’s exposure to debt fueling the artificial intelligence boom eased.  One factor depressing Nvidia stock in recent days has been nagging fears over the sustainability of debt to fund the buildout in AI.  Hyperscalers such as  Alphabet Amazon Meta  and  Microsoft  —which provide the massive cloud computing and data infrastructure behind AI—have been taking on massive debt to fund the AI buildout.

items.title: 5 S&P 500 Stocks Crank Out $4,000 Per Second Starting Now
items.summary: Investors might be unsure where to place their money this year. But some S&P 500 companies are churning out profit.

items.title: SpaceX’s High-Margin Software Business Could Soon Hit $33 Billion. Investors Are Underestimating It.
items.summary: Wall Street is fixated on SpaceX's lockup expiration while analysts quietly model a software business inside the company that could dwarf Google Cloud by 2030. Here is why the market may be pricing the wrong asset entirely.

items.title: Nvidia's plan for Wall Street could add fresh fuel — and risk — to the AI boom
items.summary: A plan for Wall Street to underwrite data center debt partially backed by Nvidia could add fresh fuel — and risk — to the AI boom.

items.title: CoreWeave Reports Solid Earnings. The Stock Jumps.
items.summary: CoreWeave’s rapid sales growth is fueled by a growing backlog, now up to $130 billion from $99 billion at the end of March.
